briefing:
T1 and T2 forecasts for 2026-02-07 have been published.

Briefing for control room (operator-focused, <250 words)

- Energy per turbine:
  - t1 energy_48h_eflh = 32.65
  - t1 energy_day_ahead_24h_eflh = 14.43
  - t2 energy_48h_eflh = 33.24
  - t2 energy_day_ahead_24h_eflh = 14.73

- Shape of the day:
  - Wind speeds moderate to strong (mean ~12.4 m/s), with highest production in the evening of 2026-02-08 (peak hour local 21:00) and a midday lull around 2026-02-08 12:00 (trough).
  - Both turbines show long stretches near rated output (t1: 10 hours, t2: 11 hours) across the 48 h window.

- Ramps and staffing:
  - Expect a notable ramp up around 2026-02-08 15:00 with a step ~0.293 of rated power for both machines. That is the main sub-hourly/operational change to monitor and could require reserve adjustments in the 1–3 hour window around that time.

- Confidence and uncertainty:
  - Confidence flagged as "low" for both turbines. Ensemble spread is moderate (mean spread ~1.97 m/s, max ~4.1 m/s) and NWP models differ (ECMWF ~11.9, GFS ~13.1, ICON ~12.3 m/s). The probabilistic bands are widened in the output (band scales ~1.12 for t1, ~1.19 for t2).
  - Recent verification shows a small persistent high bias (t1 ~0.017 over-forecast; t2 ~0.019 over-forecast over 14 days) and MAE ~0.16–0.17. Use the P10–P90 band for contingency planning rather than the single-point expectation.

- Input updates since yesterday:
  - Day-ahead hours were revised with today’s NWP runs for both turbines. Changes were material: mean absolute change ~0.073 of rated power over the overlapping 24 h, with max single-hour changes ~0.30 (t1 max 0.2973, t2 max 0.3109). Net signed change was upward (t1 +0.0255, t2 +0.0391). Plan reserves accordingly for upward revisions into the afternoon-evening window.

Operational recommendation: Hold moderate upward reserve for the 2026-02-08 afternoon-to-evening period (around 15:00–22:00 local), and be prepared for up to ~0.3 rated-power hourly swings. Rely on the P10–P90 band (published) for reserve sizing because model spread and a slight historical high bias reduce point-forecast reliability.
